events.title: Franco-Siamese Boundary Treaty
events.detail: France, then colonial ruler of Cambodia, and Siam sign a boundary treaty and accompanying map placing the Preah Vihear temple on the Cambodian side of the frontier -- the map later becomes central to ICJ rulings and the modern-day dispute.

events.title: ICJ Awards Preah Vihear Temple to Cambodia
events.detail: The International Court of Justice rules 9-3 that sovereignty over the Preah Vihear temple belongs to Cambodia, based on the 1907 French colonial-era map, but does not delineate the surrounding land border -- leaving adjacent territory contested for decades.

events.title: UNESCO Listing Triggers First Modern Clashes
events.detail: Cambodia's successful UNESCO World Heritage listing of Preah Vihear temple triggers Thai nationalist protests and the first armed skirmishes near the temple, opening a period of intermittent border clashes that runs through 2011.

events.title: 2008-2011 Preah Vihear Border Clashes
events.detail: Recurring artillery duels and troop skirmishes near Preah Vihear and Ta Krabei kill at least 20-34 people and displace thousands over three years, before Thai and Cambodian troops withdraw from the immediate temple area in 2012.

events.title: Cambodian Buildup Spotted at Hill 745
events.detail: Images emerge showing Cambodian soldiers entrenched on Hill 745 near Nam Yuen district, Ubon Ratchathani -- a disputed area -- with nearly 100 troops, a new base, and trench works reinforcing the position.

events.title: Chong Bok Clash Kills Cambodian Soldier
events.detail: Before dawn, Thai and Cambodian troops exchange fire for about 10 minutes near Chong Bok, Ubon Ratchathani, after Cambodian forces reportedly fire on a Thai liaison team sent to negotiate a troop-deployment dispute. One Cambodian soldier is killed -- the spark for the wider crisis.

events.title: Cambodia Takes Border Dispute Back to the ICJ
events.detail: Cambodia announces it will bring four contested border areas -- including sectors near Preah Vihear -- before the International Court of Justice, a move Thailand rejects, insisting on bilateral resolution through the Joint Boundary Commission.

events.title: Leaked Hun Sen Call Rocks Thai Government
events.detail: A recording surfaces of a June 15 phone call in which Thai PM Paetongtarn Shinawatra criticizes a Thai army commander and appears deferential toward Cambodia's Hun Sen while discussing the border standoff. Both governments confirm the call's authenticity, triggering a political firestorm in Bangkok.

events.title: Bhumjaithai Quits Governing Coalition
events.detail: The Bhumjaithai party, a major coalition partner, withdraws from Paetongtarn Shinawatra's government over the leaked-call scandal, stripping her administration of its comfortable parliamentary majority.

events.title: Constitutional Court Suspends PM Paetongtarn
events.detail: Thailand's Constitutional Court votes 7-2 to suspend Prime Minister Paetongtarn Shinawatra from duty pending an ethics investigation into the leaked Hun Sen call, deepening political instability just as border tensions peak.

events.title: First Landmine Blast Injures Thai Soldiers
events.detail: A landmine explosion injures Thai soldiers on patrol near the disputed border. Bangkok accuses Cambodia of freshly laying the device; Phnom Penh denies planting new mines, saying troops strayed off agreed patrol routes into old ordnance left from decades of past conflict.
events.confidenceReason: Origin of the mine (freshly laid vs. legacy ordnance) is disputed by the two governments.

events.title: Second Landmine Blast Near Chong An Ma
events.detail: A second landmine blast near the Chong An Ma crossing in Ubon Ratchathani injures five Thai soldiers, one of whom loses a leg. Thailand downgrades diplomatic relations with Cambodia within hours, recalling its ambassador -- the immediate trigger for the next day's fighting.

events.title: Fighting Erupts Along the Border, F-16s Deployed
events.detail: Clashes break out near Prasat Ta Muen Thom and spread to at least 12 border locations. The Royal Thai Air Force deploys six F-16 jets, striking Cambodian 8th and 9th Army positions -- its first combat sorties since the 1987-88 Thai-Laotian border war. Cambodian forces fire BM-21 rockets that Thai media say hit a hospital, a gas station and residential areas. Thailand declares martial law in border districts.

events.title: Death Toll Hits 32 as Fighting Enters Third Day
events.detail: The combined death toll reaches 32 with more than 130 wounded as fighting continues into a third day across border provinces on both sides; hundreds of thousands flee toward evacuation shelters.

events.title: UN Security Council Holds Closed-Door Session
events.detail: The UN Security Council convenes an urgent private meeting on the Thailand-Cambodia clashes as fighting continues into a fourth day despite mediation efforts from the US and Malaysia.

events.title: Putrajaya Ceasefire Ends Five Days of Fighting
events.detail: Thailand and Cambodia agree to an immediate ceasefire in talks hosted by Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim in Putrajaya, with US President Trump and China applying pressure via trade leverage. The five-day war killed at least 43 people (independent tallies range higher) and displaced 300,000-plus civilians.

events.title: Hun Manet Hails Ceasefire, Thailand Alleges Breach
events.detail: Cambodian PM Hun Manet calls the Putrajaya ceasefire a 'brilliant result' and thanks Anwar Ibrahim, even as the Thai military accuses Cambodian forces of continued 'indiscriminate attacks' hours after the truce took effect.

events.title: Trump Sets 19% Tariff After Ceasefire Holds
events.detail: President Trump confirms a reduced 19% US tariff rate on Thai and Cambodian goods -- down from a threatened 36% -- rewarding both governments for maintaining the ceasefire and formalizing tariff pressure as the deal's key enforcement lever.

events.title: Thai Soldiers Hurt by Landmine Amid Truce
events.detail: Three Thai soldiers are injured by a landmine blast while patrolling near the Cambodian border, testing the two-week-old ceasefire.

events.title: Thailand Again Accuses Cambodia of Laying Mines
events.detail: After another soldier is injured, Thailand formally accuses Cambodia of planting fresh landmines along the disputed frontier; Cambodia again denies the charge.

events.title: Trump Co-Signs Expanded Ceasefire at ASEAN Summit
events.detail: On the sidelines of the ASEAN Summit in Kuala Lumpur, President Trump jointly signs an expanded Thailand-Cambodia ceasefire declaration alongside Anwar Ibrahim, Anutin Charnvirakul and Hun Manet, intended to lock in de-escalation mechanisms.

events.title: Landmine Blast Prompts Thailand to Declare Truce Void
events.detail: A fresh landmine explosion injures Thai troops; Bangkok declares the ceasefire arrangement 'no longer operative,' accusing Cambodia of repeated violations and setting the stage for December's collapse.
events.confidenceReason: Precise cause of the mine incident is disputed between the two militaries.

events.title: Ceasefire Collapses, Fighting Resumes at Multiple Points
events.detail: The mid-2025 ceasefire arrangement formally breaks down as fighting resumes at more than a dozen points along the border, with both sides accusing the other of provoking the renewed clashes.

events.title: Death Toll Climbs as Hostilities Flare Anew
events.detail: Renewed border hostilities push casualty figures higher within days of the collapse, with fighter-jet sorties, rocket fire and artillery exchanges reported along nearly every border province on both sides.

events.title: Thai PM Anutin Dissolves Parliament
events.detail: PM Anutin Charnvirakul dissolves the House of Representatives, triggering a snap election within 45-60 days -- a move seen as anchoring the coming campaign on a nationalist response to the border crisis while averting a no-confidence vote.

events.title: Civilian Killed as Border Clashes Continue
events.detail: A civilian is killed in renewed cross-border shelling as the second phase of fighting continues, adding to a mounting civilian toll on both sides.

events.title: Renewed Fighting Batters Trat Province Economy
events.detail: Thailand's Trat province reports tourism losses of at least 300 million baht ($9.6M), with total economic losses exceeding 1 billion baht ($32M) in nine days, as renewed clashes empty border towns of visitors.

events.title: China Offers to Help Resolve the Rift
events.detail: Beijing publicly offers to mediate between Bangkok and Phnom Penh as fighting drags on, part of a broader push by China to position itself as a stabilizing regional power alongside ASEAN and the US.

events.title: Cambodian Civilian Death Toll Reaches 21 on Day 17
events.detail: On the 17th day of renewed fighting, Cambodia's reported civilian death toll rises to 21, with dozens more wounded, as displacement across Cambodia's northern provinces continues to grow.

events.title: Second Ceasefire Signed at Chanthaburi Border Crossing
events.detail: Defence ministers Natthaphon Narkphanit (Thailand) and Tea Seiha (Cambodia) sign a renewed ceasefire at Ban Pak Kard crossing, Chanthaburi, at the 3rd Special GBC meeting, ending 20 days of fighting that killed at least 101 people and displaced more than half a million. ASEAN observers, led by the Philippines, deploy to monitor compliance.

events.title: Thailand Reports Hundreds of Cambodian Drone Incursions
events.detail: Just two days after the new truce, Thailand accuses Cambodia of violating the ceasefire with hundreds of drone incursions over Thai territory; Cambodia disputes the characterization.
events.confidenceReason: Scale and intent of the alleged incursions are disputed by Cambodia.

events.title: China, Cambodia, Thailand Hold Trilateral FM Meeting
events.detail: Foreign ministers of China, Cambodia and Thailand hold a trilateral meeting to reinforce the new ceasefire and discuss follow-up mechanisms, underscoring Beijing's expanding mediating role.

events.title: Thailand Frees 18 Cambodian Soldiers
events.detail: Thailand releases 18 Cambodian soldiers held since the July clashes after the ceasefire holds past the agreed 72-hour threshold, a confidence-building step under the December 27 deal.

events.title: 409,000 Remain Displaced Despite Ceasefire
events.detail: A World Vision situation report finds roughly 409,000 people still displaced across Thailand and Cambodia, with the largest concentrations in Siem Reap and Banteay Meanchey provinces, even as numbers gradually decline post-ceasefire.

events.title: Cambodia Demands Thai Troop Withdrawal
events.detail: Cambodia's foreign ministry protests alleged continued Thai military presence inside disputed territory, demanding withdrawal a week into the new truce.

events.title: Thailand Says Disputed Border Strike Was Accidental
events.detail: Cambodia alleges a new Thai strike on its territory; the Thai military characterizes the incident as accidental rather than a deliberate ceasefire breach, illustrating how fragile the truce remains.
events.confidenceReason: Thailand disputes Cambodia's characterization of the strike as deliberate.

events.title: Hun Manet Announces Recovery Measures, Thanks China
events.detail: Cambodian PM Hun Manet unveils government measures to address the conflict's economic and humanitarian toll, publicly thanking China for its diplomatic and economic support during the crisis.

events.title: Cambodia Alleges Ten Days of Ceasefire Violations
events.detail: Cambodia's government accuses Thailand of violating the truce between January 12 and 22; Thailand's Joint Information Centre denies the claims, saying it has adhered strictly to the agreed Troop Deployment Line from the December 27 GBC statement.
events.confidenceReason: Thailand and Cambodia give directly conflicting accounts of the same period.

events.title: Bhumjaithai Wins Snap Election on Nationalist Wave
events.detail: Thailand's snap general election delivers a landslide to PM Anutin Charnvirakul's Bhumjaithai party (193 seats), with the People's Party second (120) and Paetongtarn's Pheu Thai a distant third (74) -- the first 21st-century win for an avowedly nationalist platform, powered by the party's hardline border stance.

events.title: Hun Manet Says Thai Forces Occupy 'Deep' Territory
events.detail: Cambodian PM Hun Manet tells international media that Thai forces have pushed into long-held Cambodian territory beyond the agreed line of dispute despite the ceasefire, reiterating Cambodia's preference for peaceful, legal resolution over renewed conflict.
events.confidenceReason: Thailand disputes Cambodia's account of troop positions relative to the agreed deployment line.

events.title: Thailand and Cambodia Exchange Fire in Sisaket
events.detail: Cambodian forces fire a single 40mm grenade round near a Thai patrol in Sisaket province; Thai troops return fire. No Thai personnel are reported injured, but the incident underscores how easily the ceasefire can still be tested.

era: Mar-Aug 2026: Fences, MOU 44, and Great-Power Mediation

events.title: Thailand Announces Border Fence Construction Plan
events.detail: Thailand announces it will begin building fencing along sections of its 817km frontier with Cambodia, part of a shift from active fighting toward long-term 'structural encroachment' -- infrastructure meant to fix contested lines on the ground.

events.title: Pilot Fence Segment Rises in Chanthaburi
events.detail: Thailand completes a 1.3km pilot fence segment of reinforced concrete panels topped with steel mesh and concertina wire between border markers 52-54 in Chanthaburi province, with plans for at least 7km more where terrain allows.

events.title: Cambodia Demands JBC Approval for Fence Alignment
events.detail: Cambodia says it does not object to Thailand building fencing within its own territory but insists any alignment near disputed sectors must be agreed through the Joint Boundary Committee, rejecting unilateral Thai maps of the frontier.

events.title: Thailand Formally Withdraws From MOU 44
events.detail: The Thai Cabinet authorizes unilateral withdrawal from the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU 44) governing joint maritime boundary and oil/gas talks with Cambodia -- a campaign pledge PM Anutin fulfills after the February election. Cambodia calls it counter to the deal's original spirit and signals it will pursue compulsory UNCLOS conciliation.

events.title: Cambodia Brings ASEAN Observers to Disputed Frontier
events.detail: Cambodia escorts the ASEAN Observer Team on an inspection of disputed sectors of the Thai frontier, part of ongoing monitoring efforts under the December 2025 ceasefire framework.

events.title: Xi Jinping Offers to Facilitate Thailand-Cambodia Talks
events.detail: Meeting separately with Thai PM Anutin and Cambodian PM Hun Manet, Chinese President Xi Jinping offers to play a 'constructive role' in resolving the border dispute, extending Beijing's mediation push and reinforcing China's bid for regional security influence under its Global Security Initiative.

events.title: Thailand Presses On With Fence Despite Cambodian Objections
events.detail: A year after the deadliest clashes, Thailand continues extending border fencing and infrastructure in disputed sectors, while Cambodia maintains that any permanent construction requires joint demarcation first.

events.title: Thailand Approves 433.5M Baht for Border Shelters
events.detail: Thailand's Cabinet approves 433.5 million baht in emergency funding for 1,669 shelters and improved warning/communication systems across seven border provinces, formalizing longer-term civil-defense infrastructure along the frontier.

events.title: Anutin Visits Disputed Hill 500 at Chong An Ma
events.detail: PM Anutin Charnvirakul visits Thai troops at Hill 500 near the Chong An Ma crossing, the site of an August 17 landmine blast. Thailand says the visit stayed within its administered territory; Cambodia disputes the location entirely, calling it An Seh within its own Preah Vihear province.

events.title: Cambodia Files Formal Protest Over An Seh Visit
events.detail: Cambodia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs formally protests Anutin's August 23 visit, calling it an unauthorized attempt to assert an illegitimate claim over Cambodian sovereign territory and demanding Thailand cease activities in the area.

events.title: Anutin Dismisses Cambodia's Call to Arrest Him
events.detail: Anutin brushes off Cambodian commentary urging authorities to seek an arrest warrant against him over the Hill 500/An Seh visit, saying he acted lawfully under the December 2025 Joint Statement.
